The compiler lets you call an `any` with any arguments. It does not check that the value is a function, and the result is `any` again. If the value is not a function, you find out from a `TypeError` when the code runs.

The rule reports calls, `new`, and tagged templates. It also reports a value of type `Function`, which says that something can be called but not with what. A type that cannot be resolved, for example from a missing import, counts as `any`.

This rule needs type information. Run `bun lint --type-aware`. With that flag, it is on by default in TypeScript files.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 4} */}
```ts
function run(plugin: any, handler: Function) {
  plugin();
  plugin.setup();
  new plugin.Worker();
  handler();
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
interface Plugin {
  setup(): void;
  Worker: new () => object;
}

function run(plugin: Plugin, handler: () => void) {
  plugin.setup();
  new plugin.Worker();
  handler();
}
```

For a value you know nothing about, use `unknown` and check it before the call:

{/* good */}
```ts
function stop(controller: unknown) {
  if (controller instanceof AbortController) {
    controller.abort();
  }
}
```

## When not to use it

In a codebase that is still moving from JavaScript to TypeScript, `any` is everywhere and the reports drown out the rest. Turn the rule on once most values have real types.
